paper.title: A C. elegans mutant that lives twice as long as wild type

organism.source_quote: We have found that mutations in the gene daf-2 can cause fertile, active, adult Caenorhabditis elegans hermaphrodites to live more than twice as long as wild type.

experiments.notes: Abstract-only labeling: full text paywalled (Nature 1993). Effect magnitude reported as 'more than twice as long' (>100%) but the statistic (median/mean/max) is not specified in the abstract, so all _change_pct fields are null per the mean-vs-median guideline. daf-2 allele not named in abstract. The extension requires daf-16 activity (epistasis), recorded here rather than as mechanism because the abstract states a genetic requirement, not a mechanism of action. Both genes also regulate dauer larva formation.
